sentences.text: Researchers scanned rats using fMRI three to six days after intermittent alcohol exposure, grouping subjects by whether they began drinking as adolescents or adults.

By analyzing activity correlations across trials, they found that adolescent-onset rats displayed stronger communication between the medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices when reacting to ethanol smells.
However, this specific connectivity difference was no longer statistically significant after accounting for abstinence duration, and consumption level alone did not yield significant changes.

Conversely, heavy adolescent drinkers exhibited weaker connections between the prelimbic and anterior cingulate cortex, as well as reduced amygdala-insula connectivity, which remained significant after adjustments.
The authors conclude that these changes may reflect developmental differences, alcohol effects, or both, indicating adolescence is a critical period for processing alcohol cues.
